Admission, This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 with their counsel Shri Pruthvi K.S. and complainant-PW.1 Reshma Manjunatha Naik with counsel Shri Mohankumar M, who filed power today for complainant are present before the Court.
2. Learned HCGP for respondent-State present.

3. Petitioners and PW.1-complainant submit that they have settled their disputes between them and filed joint compromise petition under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure.
4. Parties who are present before the Court have been identified by their respective counsel.

5. Petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 3 were tried before the trial Court on the file of J.M.F.C, Ankola in C.C.No.423/2003 for the offence punishable under Section 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The trail Court after appreciation of evidence has convicted the accused for both offences, but imposed sentence only for the offence under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC.

The said judgment of conviction and order of sentence was assailed before First Appellate Court on the file of Manjunath S/O Vishnu Naik vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125809261/

sentences.text: The First Appellate Court by it's judgment dated 16.09.2021 dismissed the appeal and confirmed the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the trial Court.
6. The concurrent findings have been assailed by the revision petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 3 before this Court.
It is now submitted that PW.1 and revision petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 3 have compromised their disputes amongst themselves amicably.
PW.1-Reshma Manjunatha Naik submits that she has no objection for compounding the offence, since they have compromised the matter and settled their disputes amicably.
7. The compromise petition filed by parties under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C, is hereby recorded.
The matter is essentially arising out of domestic relationship between the parties and as the same has already been settled between the parties, there is no legal impediment to quash the proceedings.

8. At this stage, it is worth to note the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Gian Singh vs State Of Punjab & Another reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court held that offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile, civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute, High Court may quash the criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Gian Singh vs State Of Punjab & Another reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. The question is as to whether the compromise petition can be accepted in the present revision petition.

10. In the aforesaid judgment of Gian Singh, the appeal was pending before Sessions Court and the application for compounding the offence was filed which was ordered to be taken along with main appeal.
Therefore, petitioner filed petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing the F.I.R on the ground of compounding offence.
The said petition came to be dismissed by the High Court.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C can be exercised by the High Court to quash the proceedings where the parties have settled their disputes amicably amongst themselves.

11. In the circumstances of the case and in view of the fact that parties have amicably settled their disputes, so also in the light of guidelines given by Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid decision, I am of the opinion that factual aspects of this case also falls within the categories of guidelines given by Hon'ble Apex Court.
Therefore, there is no legal impediment to quash the proceedings in the said criminal case as prayed for.

Consequently, proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The joint petition filed under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure by revision petitioners and PW.1-complainant Smt. Reshma Manjunatha Naik is hereby accepted.
Consequently, judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by trial Court which is confirmed by First Appellate Court are hereby set-aside in view of parties settling their disputes amicably.
